subject: Performance evaluation sprint: burst vs steady-flow tests & MAP timeline
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Martin <susan.martin@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance evaluation sprint: burst vs steady-flow tests & MAP timeline

Hi Susan,

Following our discovery call last week, attaching a first-draft MAP and proposed performance test plan so we can align on acceptance criteria for the POC. High-level asks from Acme we captured:
- Validate burst safety up to 1k concurrent requests per region and steady-state at 250 rps
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) targets for short prompts: P50 < 300ms, P95 < 900ms
- Queueing behavior / tail latency under synthetic load and real prefix reuse patterns

Proposed schedule (draft):
- Aug 4–5: onboarding & baseline profiling (small dataset, single region)
- Aug 6–8: burst vs steady-state runs across 3 session profiles
- Aug 9: delivery of raw results + debrief

Files: acme_map_v1.xlsx (MAP with responsibilities / milestones), perf-test-plan.yaml (test harness config).

Please confirm the acceptance targets above and any additional constraints (e.g., token budgets, sensitive prompt sets). If that looks good I’ll lock the schedule and book the dedicated test window.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: acme_map_v1.xlsx (xlsx), perf-test-plan.yaml (yaml)

From: Susan Martin <susan.martin@acme-enterprises.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-enterprises.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance evaluation sprint: burst vs steady-flow tests & MAP timeline

Hi Sofia — thanks, this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:

1) Concurrency: 1k concurrent is our peak target but it must include real-world burst shading from our front-end (we typically see sub-second spikes when new campaigns start). Please simulate both synchronized bursts (all clients start within 2s) and staggered bursts (jitter up to 200ms).

2) TTFT targets: P50 < 300ms is required for internal UX tests; P95 < 1s is acceptable but anything >1s will be a blocker for the demo.

3) Rate-limits and graceful degradation: we need documented behavior when the system hits soft vs hard rate-limits. Do you expose queue depth metrics and per-token billing for cached vs uncached responses?

4) Data security: any logs from the runs that contain prompt text must be redacted or stored in our tenant-only bucket.

We are okay with the proposed Aug 6–8 test window but can shift if you need more time to tune the rate limiter. Also please include a short sample prompt set — we’ll mark anything sensitive.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Martin
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Enterprises

Quick internal note / directions:

- Prioritize instrumenting queue-depth and tokenized-cache-hit metrics. Add the following tags to the test harness: region, model_variant, cache_hit (true/false), request_length_bucket.
- Start the first burst run at 10:00 PDT on Aug 6 with a small canary (50 concurrent) to validate the traffic generator and metric hooks. If canary is green (no error rate >0.5% and no queue depth > 80), escalate to full burst.
- Configure soft rate-limit at 250 rps per model instance group and hard limit at 1.2k rps cluster-wide. Soft limit should return 429 with Retry-After and a suggested pre-warm header; hard limit should drop requests and log a distinct error for postmortem.
- For demo safety, prepare a fallback model variant that is 2x cheaper to run; configure automatic fallback on sustained P95 tail >1.2s.

Also loop Legal if Acme wants persistent raw prompt logs. Neha, please confirm we can redact before handing over any textual logs.

Rishi
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Martin <susan.martin@acme-enterprises.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance evaluation sprint: burst vs steady-flow tests & MAP timeline

Susan / Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround. We ran the planned matrix of tests (attached CSV) and here are the highlights up front:

- Burst safety: full synchronized bursts to 1k concurrent completed with error rate 0.4% (failures were transient 5xx from an overloaded instance, all retried successfully by client-side logic). Queue depth spiked to 92 for ~14s during the peak synchronized start.
- Steady-state: sustained 250 rps profile kept P95 latency at 760ms, P50 at 220ms.
- TTFT: short prompts achieved P50 270ms, P95 880ms.
- Rate-limit behavior: soft rate-limit returned 429+Retry-After as planned; we recorded per-instance Retry-After distribution and included the header suggestion for pre-warm. Hard limit was never reached in this matrix.

Action items:
- We’ll redact prompt text and share a sanitized export to your tenant bucket by EOD Aug 11 (Neha leading).
- Neha will produce a short playbook for rate-limit tuning (recommended soft thresholds per region and guidance for client retry windows).
- Rishi suggested we prepare a fallback model variant config for the demo; engineering has a quantized 7B candidate ready for validation.

Attachments: perf-results-2026-08-09.csv (summary rows + raw samples), link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/open?id=1A2b3C_acme-perf-report

Next step: propose a 45-min results walk-through on Aug 12 or 13; please share preferred times.

—
Sofia

Redwood Inference
